expectations.text: In the rendered DOM for both English and Finnish, every number-unit pair in the table (weight, battery, storage, display, battery life, price) is joined by U+00A0 or U+202F, never a plain U+0020
expectations.evidence: Rendered textContent, EN and FI: every number-unit pair uses U+00A0 (e.g. 1.24|U+00A0|kg, 13,6|U+00A0|tuumaa, 1|U+00A0|299|U+00A0|€); EN price is a prefix symbol with no separator ("€1,299"), no U+0020 anywhere.

expectations.text: The Finnish rendering uses decimal commas (1,24 and 99,5) and groups the prices with a no-break space (1 299 €)
expectations.evidence: FI render: "1,24 kg", "99,5 Wh", price "1 299 €" with code points 1|U+00A0|2|9|9|U+00A0|U+20AC.

expectations.text: specs.html sets the numeric cells with tabular-nums
expectations.evidence: table { font-variant-numeric: lining-nums tabular-nums; }; computed on every td: "lining-nums tabular-nums".

expectations.text: specs.html sets the html lang attribute to fi when Finnish is selected
expectations.evidence: After clicking the page's Suomi button, document.documentElement.lang === "fi" (render() sets document.documentElement.lang = lang).

expectations.text: specs.html uses logical properties for text layout (no margin-left/right, padding-left/right, text-align: left/right, left/right offsets)
expectations.evidence: CSS uses margin-inline, padding-inline(-start/-end), text-align: start/end, inline-size; only physical items are uniform shorthands (margin: 0, padding: 2px) and an overflow-x fallback; no left/right properties.

expectations.text: In the rendered DOM for both languages, the battery-life qualifier (up to / jopa) is bound to its number with a no-break space, so it cannot be stranded at a line end
expectations.evidence: Rendered: EN "up|U+00A0|to|U+00A0|18|U+00A0|h", FI "jopa|U+00A0|18|U+00A0|h"; all three cells per language.
